title: A Bag of Tricks for Automated De Novo Design of Molecules with the Desired Properties: Application to EGFR Inhibitor Discovery
summary: A deep recurrent generator with reinforcement learning nominated EGFR compounds; enzyme assays confirmed 4 of 15 predicted actives, including two with nanomolar potency. Five predicted-inactive controls were inactive. This is a small preclinical proof of concept.
ai_technology: Generative recurrent neural network with reinforcement learning
organization: Carnegie Mellon University; University of Oxford; University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

evidence.tested: The v1 preprint reports four confirmed inhibitors among 15 assayed predicted actives and five inactive predicted-inactive controls. Two predicted-active compounds were insoluble and not assayed. Two hits had nanomolar inhibition comparable to staurosporine; the selected-batch hit fraction does not establish a general success rate.
evidence.unknown: The result is a proof-of-concept assay on 15 predicted actives and five predicted-inactive controls. The preprint does not establish therapeutic efficacy or generalize its hit rate beyond this target and protocol.
evidence.ai_role: A deep recurrent neural network generated SMILES molecules; reinforcement learning used an EGFR random-forest activity predictor with transfer learning, experience replay and reward shaping to guide generation and selection.

source_review.scope: Original ChemRxiv v1 PDF initial sections plus indexed primary assay/summary passages and official version metadata; complete PDF not independently re-read.
